nodes.label: The repository layout
nodes.rationale: Each directory has a rule for putting something there rather than a description: kernel/ is what must run at EL1 or defines the isolation boundary; user/lib/ is what more than one program needs; tools/ is what runs on your desk, not on the target.

nodes.label: arch/ is which processor, hal/ is which board
nodes.rationale: A Pi 5 and QEMU's virt are both AArch64 - same arch/, different hal/. A Pi 1 is ARMv6 - different arch/ and different hal/.

nodes.label: The running-system layout
nodes.rationale: Modelled on BeOS's hard line between what the system ships and what a person accumulates: /system, /user, /home, /dev, /tmp. BeOS put the first under /boot/beos and the second under /boot/home, and you could delete the second without breaking the machine.

nodes.label: No /boot prefix
nodes.rationale: BeOS had one because the boot volume was one of several mounted disks. Here the layout is the namespace, so a prefix naming the volume it came from would describe something a process cannot see anyway.

nodes.label: bin split into programs and applications
nodes.rationale: A program prints and reads lines, an application opens a window. /bin today holds both and the Deskbar has to filter it by reading a manifest line out of every file.

nodes.label: The layout is a convention, not a tree
nodes.rationale: Nothing walks from /. Init assembles the layout and hands out different subsets: a game started from the Deskbar gets /system/libraries, /app/wm and /home/settings, and cannot open your documents - not because it is forbidden but because /home was never put in its namespace.

nodes.label: tools/kfs.lua on the host
nodes.rationale: A disk this Mac cannot mount is still a disk this Mac can write. build/host/lua runs kfs.lua unchanged, so the same code that formats a disk inside the machine can populate an image outside it - the step that unblocks fonts, wallpapers, a WAD and moving /bin out of the binary.

nodes.label: run_interchange.py
nodes.rationale: Writes a file on the host, reads it inside the machine, writes one inside the machine and reads it back - because a format only one of the two can write is a format that traps everything you make in it.

nodes.label: Every process is the same ELF with a different role number
nodes.rationale: Init, the shell, a server and an application are one binary entered at different places. Making /system/servers/disk a real loaded file means an ELF loader for user processes, which does not exist.

nodes.label: There is no dynamic linking
nodes.rationale: No dlopen, no shared objects. A C library is linked into whoever uses it, so /system/libraries can hold Lua libraries and cannot hold C ones. C system libraries are a build-time fact, not a filesystem one.

nodes.label: The order this suggests
nodes.rationale: Rename to the convention; a host image builder using kfs.lua; move fonts and assets to the disk, reclaiming most of the 19.6 MB the image costs across fourteen processes; move /bin and /lib to the disk; an ELF loader, which is also what Doom needs.
